name: Valacyclovir
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Valacyclovir is converted to acyclovir, which the kidneys clear. The US label reduces doses at creatinine clearance (CrCl) below 50 mL/min by indication and gives the dose after hemodialysis.

bands.recommendation: CrCl 30–49: herpes zoster 1 g every 12 hours; cold sores two 1 g doses 12 hours apart; genital herpes regimens unchanged (label).

CrCl 10–29: herpes zoster 1 g every 24 hours; cold sores two 500 mg doses 12 hours apart; initial genital herpes 1 g every 24 hours; recurrent 500 mg every 24 hours; suppression 500 mg every 24 hours (500 mg every 48 hours for the ≤9 recurrences/year alternative) (label).

CrCl 10–29 as above; CrCl <10: herpes zoster 500 mg every 24 hours; cold sores 500 mg single dose; initial genital herpes 500 mg every 24 hours; recurrent and suppression 500 mg every 24 hours (500 mg every 48 hours alternative) (label).

hd.text: Give the recommended dose after hemodialysis; about one-third of acyclovir is removed in a 4-hour session (label).

pd.text: No specific information; acyclovir removal by CAPD is less than by hemodialysis and kinetics resemble end-stage kidney disease (label). Use the CrCl <10 regimen; specialist input.

crrt.text: Label notes CAVHD removes less acyclovir than hemodialysis; no dosing. Specialist input.

dialyzable: Yes: about one-third removed in a 4-hour hemodialysis session (label).
monitoring: Neurotoxicity (confusion, hallucinations) and acute kidney injury risk higher in kidney impairment and older adults; hydration.

pediatric.approved_ages: Cold sores: 12 years and older. Chickenpox: 2 to <18 years. Not established for genital herpes or herpes zoster under 18 years (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Chickenpox: 20 mg/kg 3 times daily for 5 days. Cold sores (12 years and older): 2 g every 12 hours for 1 day (label).
pediatric.max_dose: Chickenpox: not to exceed 1 g 3 times daily (label).

renal.recommendation: No data in pediatric patients with CrCl <50 mL/min/1.73 m2 (label). Specialist input.
No data in pediatric patients with CrCl <50 mL/min/1.73 m2 (label). Specialist input.
No data in pediatric patients with CrCl <50 mL/min/1.73 m2 (label). Specialist input.

pediatric.neonates: Neonates: not established (including suppression after neonatal herpes simplex infection) (label).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
